## Overview
### Introduction to Google: Nano Banana 2
The Google: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview) is a cutting-edge language model developed by Google, released on January 1, 2024. As a standard-tier model, it is not open-source. This model is designed to handle a wide range of tasks, including text generation, coding, analysis, and summarization, making it a versatile tool for developers. With its capabilities in text, function calling, JSON mode, streaming, and structured outputs, it can be applied to various use cases such as chat, text generation, and RAG pipelines.

### Architecture and Strengths
The architecture of Google: Nano Banana 2 is built around a context window of 65,536 tokens, allowing it to process and understand large amounts of text. It also has a maximum output limit of 65,536 tokens, making it suitable for generating extensive text content. The model's knowledge cutoff is December 2023, ensuring it has access to a vast amount of knowledge up to that point. In terms of pricing, the model charges $0.5 per 1M tokens for input and $3.0 per 1M tokens for output. Its strengths are reflected in its benchmark scores, including an MMLU score of 80.0 and an LMSYS Arena ELO score of 1200, indicating its high performance in various linguistic tasks.

### Use Cases and Cost Examples
